items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: I listen to recordings of Cannonball Adderley talking to the audience.

ctx.x: who are self-editing and I’m not sure what my point is but I feel a little sorry for the younger musicians because those gigs seem to be fewer and farther between these days.

But this is something that I think — I talk to my students about — because last night it was great because yesterday I had a young man playing bass with me that’s a student at the University. Because my two bass players were out of town, so I called this young man who’s from the state, he’s from Montpelier. And this is — he’s going into his senior year now at UVM and I got him on the gig and I got him on because I figured great time, come on in, figure out what’s going on, I kind of just guided him through what…

here I went to see some of the young cats playing and I told them man the music that you’re playing is the kind of music that you’re going to have seven guys in the audience going, “Hey man wow, ‘Giant Steps’ in seven man, that’s really hip man.” And I would tell them yeah that’s real cool but you know the average person on the street, they’re not going to get it and they’re not going to be there to listen to that. I think jazz in general has always been a people music but it’s getting to the point where we’re…
